harness.name: production-c-serial1-workers1-two
limits: Collector delivery adds latency to attachment observation; app elapsed and host monotonic origins differ.
One fresh process; SQLite may already be running.
Draft latency ends when the controlled marker is visible on the reconstructed terminal screen, not when raw contiguous bytes occur.
Includes SSH transport and output delivery; establishes neither physical presentation nor CPU causality.
No screen rows or unrelated terminal text are exported; failed echo/clear waits are censored without retries.

qualifiers: Use one boot per byte window; IDs can repeat after reboot.

Full/missed counters qualify incomplete coverage; expiration removes observation only and never cancels disk work.
Released counts dropped observation owners; absence or a release count alone never proves disk completion.
Rows are sampled snapshots; brief phases may be missed and BSP starvation may suppress samples.

catalog_failure.cause_limit: DNS, TLS, network service placement, and timer causes are not established by the fixed send-error categories. Both matched-B and production-C sixth alias preludes on initial carrier15 show this separate pre-download failure.

observation.reason: The current-end snapshot included the separately launched retry context request7; it cannot classify the earlier sixth alias attempt.

outcomes.interpretation: The production BSP-required I/O service policy preserves progress through the previously reproducible fifth-Codex carrier14 read stall. All six actual Codex processes reached ready and accepted a cleared draft. The sixth ordinary alias attempt failed catalog connect before Codex download, so this is not six consecutive alias successes. Seconds of early draft latency remain.

observation.scope: Six offline protocol fixtures with subprocess and HTTP entry points patched to reject calls.

limits: One rig, one production-kernel boot, six actual Codex starts; broader hardware, prompt, model-response and long-session behavior were not validated.
Original strict six-alias manifest remains false; a separately named seventh alias attempt supplied the sixth actual Codex process only after the failed catalog prelude fully retired.
The sixth-alias current-end snapshot overlapped the separate retry; it is excluded. Only the explicit pre-retry endpoint55151567 classifies that failed attempt.
Screen latency includes SSH transport and delivery; it does not isolate application CPU time or physical screen presentation.
Host loader monotonic and application elapsed clocks have different origins and are not blindly added.
Sampled native-FS phases are sparse and bounded. Absence, observer expiry, and released-owner counters alone do not prove I/O completion.
Prior exact-generation retirement proofs establish filesystem/native drain and carrier release at their observed endpoints; serialized caller control is still required.
The placement change addresses the demonstrated disk-service dependency. Early input latency and repeated sixth-alias catalog connect failure remain separate production-readiness work.
Collector windows are fixed against one append-only file identity. File metadata does not attest remote kernel memory or detect arbitrary in-place collector rewrites.
